design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER — task 1 (rebuild_contracts_and_draws), rework round 11. Draw: prerequisite_problems=2, factor_counts=[5,5,5]; each of rebuild_ext_deductive_signature, rebuild_ext_overdue_draw_charge and rebuild_ext_draw_payoff takes 5.

WHY A GOOD TEST. A San Antonio property manager (Dana Larkin) says the crew stopped over the overdue drywall draw and wants to pay what is due so work resumes. The payment rule waits on the overdue charge owed for each owed calendar-month fee period (October: due 2026-09-24, grace to 2026-10-04, first charge day 2026-10-05) and on no deductive proposal awaiting signature (co 3, 100 sq ft of drywall the owner removed); the charge rule itself waits on the deductive signature. The agent finds the chain signature -> charge -> payment, prices each with five factors and hands two writes to the customer.

SCOPE. Claimed: rebuild_ext_deductive_signature (sign_deductive_change_order_5bfd6b95, user), rebuild_ext_overdue_draw_charge (post_overdue_draw_charge_f6859441, agent), rebuild_ext_draw_payoff (pay_past_due_draw_ec4ba96a, user).

PROBLEM-TREE CARD. Root rebuild_ext_draw_payoff. Edges: charge -> signature (value_input, credit_set_off, state, negated: "The overdue draw charge for a fee period is not fixed until no deductive change order proposal stands on the contract awaiting the customer's signature; a deductive proposal whose credit worked out under the deductive change order signature rule is nothing is not counted, because it cannot be written."); payment -> charge (value_input, overdue_carried: "... only after the records carry the overdue draw charge owed on that draw for each calendar month fee period that is owed; a fee period owes no overdue draw charge, and no charge is recorded for it, when the amounts set against the balance the charge is figured on are at least that balance."); payment -> signature (value_input, credit_applied: "The past-due payment is fixed only after no deductive change order proposal remains on the contract awaiting the customer's signature; a deductive proposal whose credit worked out under the deductive change order signature rule is nothing is not counted, because it cannot be written."). Each condition equals its sentence. Order: signature (9), charge (14), payment (17). Deletion runs: skip signature -> charge 85.33, payment 7169.82; skip charge -> payment 6667.44. Under the payment rule's declared overwrite of the base resumption sentence, the draw counts as paid in full once this payment posts, so work resumes later and the remobilization fee the payment carries is booked then; the resumption is the crew's return on a later date, not a write owed during the call.

FACTOR CARD — deductive credit (423.40; baseline 286.00): dc_carrier_price (method, cross claims) drywall added by the insurance_scope change order under supplement 1: 1,762.80 / 520 = 3.39, credited on the 100 sq ft change-order part (all within the 520 sq ft change order 1 added; contract part 0); baseline 359.80. dc_overhead_return (param, cross claims) 20%, mirroring the overhead and profit charged on the insurance_scope addition; baseline 337.00. dc_treatment_return (param, cross water) 0.41 x 100; baseline 374.20. dc_cleaning_return (param, cross water) HEPA 0.52 x 100; baseline 361.00. dc_processing_deduction (param) construction started -> 95.00 (company schedule); baseline 518.40.
FACTOR CARD — overdue charge (78.98; baseline 210.57): ov_balance_days (method) 22-day charge span from the first charge day, 10 days at the balance before the 2026-10-14 payment and 12 at the balance now; baseline 95.14. ov_credit_application (method) 423.40; baseline 85.33. ov_owner_retention (param) 2,203.827 (no completion yet); baseline 112.04. ov_depreciation_pending (param, cross claims) 3,884.60 withheld until completion; baseline 137.25. ov_supplement_pending (param, cross claims) supplement 2 undecided, 1,184.00; baseline 96.74.
FACTOR CARD — payment (6746.42; baseline 14038.27): py_overdue_carried 78.98 (charges on the paid draw); baseline 6667.44. py_credit_applied (method) 423.40; baseline 7169.82. py_owner_retention 2,203.827; baseline 8950.25. py_remobilization 325.00; baseline 6421.42. py_carrier_pending 3,884.60 + 1,184.00 set aside; baseline 11815.02.

BASE-INVARIANT CARD. Signature: ch_state, co_signed. Charge: od_customer, od_grace (due 2026-09-24 + 10 days; first charge 2026-10-05; frozen 2026-10-26). Payment: pp_state; ACH tender.

SEED. Homeowner Direct Pay claim (trades 4): initial dwelling approval 56,860.00 withholding 3,884.60 depreciation (2026-06-01), ACV 56,860.00 - 3,884.60 - 2,500.00 = 50,475.40 paid to the insured alone 2026-06-05, supplement 1 approved 1,762.80 on 2026-08-10 and paid to the insured 2026-08-14, supplement 2 (scope omission, 1,184.00) delivered 2026-10-19 with no carrier decision yet, no depreciation release (180-day window open), carrier receivable 6,384.60; Black Water Standard water job (category_3, closed); contract 52,400.00 built 1985, permit 2026-07-10, construction 2026-07-15, suspended 2026-10-16; co 1 insurance_scope drywall 520 sq ft naming supplement 1, booked 2,695.68 under the rule in force; co 2 owner upgrade 1,604.25; co 3 deductive drywall pending, no supplement named; draws 10,000.00 (paid in full) and 22,038.27 (due 2026-09-24, 8,000.00 paid 2026-10-14).

STANDARD SOLUTION. locate/verify -> contract -> change orders -> claim file -> requests -> approvals -> water job -> hand deductive signature (423.40) -> draws -> payments -> claim payments -> post October charge 78.98 -> charges -> hand payment (draw 2, ach, 6746.42).

VERIFICATION. /tmp verify.py with the real tools reproduces every figure; probe table in the worklog; gates green.

REVISIONS. Round 4: C-02, R2-06, R3-01, R3-05(b) closed for this task (worklog REWORK round 4); the claim-pending set-off left the policies for the carrier-money tier. Round 6: R5-01 closed — the overdue charge's timing is one convention per date (chargeable days on the due date, days at the current balance on the latest payment date), combined once; the charge and the payment moved. Round 9: one balance convention owns the charge span and the payments (ov_balance_days), the carrier-money set-off splits into recoverable depreciation and supplement money (supplement 2 seeded undecided), Texas retention applies only until the statutory days after completion; the charge and the payment moved. Round 11: the deductive credit mirrors the additive pricing (quantity written, carrier price, treatment, framing cleaning, the markup charged on the addition); the seeded insurance_scope change order, its charge line and the drywall draw were re-priced under the rules in force; the credit, the charge and the payment moved.
user_scenario:
You are Dana Larkin, a principal at Larkin & Moore Property Management in San Antonio. Your firm manages a mid-size apartment portfolio, and Unit 6 at 4511 Broadway St is being rebuilt by Ridgecrest after a water loss in May. You are friendly, efficient and slightly apologetic: the owner's accounts payable was slow on the drywall draw. You are calling from your desk on a Monday morning.

You start by saying the crew stopped work on the Broadway Unit 6 rebuild last week over the overdue drywall draw, that you sent part of it on the fourteenth, and that you want to pay whatever is due on that draw today so the crew can come back. You will make the payment yourself on this call through whatever payment step they give you; you only want the representative to tell you the amount and set it up. You do not want anything else changed on the contract.

You share details only when asked. If asked for a phone number, it is 2105550362. If asked for an email, it is dana.larkin@larkinmoorepm.com. If asked for a ZIP code, the billing ZIP is 78209. If asked which property, it is Unit 6 at 4511 Broadway St. If asked how you will pay, you pay by ACH from the owner's operating account; you never read out account numbers over the phone. If asked about the earlier payment, you remember sending eight thousand dollars by ACH on October 14 but would rather the representative read the exact records. If asked about insurance, the carrier paid the owner directly. If asked about anything else on the account, you say you would like them to go by what the records show.

If the representative tells you there is something on the contract waiting for your signature, you ask what it is; once they explain it, you say the owner did decide to keep that plaster wall as it is, and you agree to sign it. When they hand you that signing step, you run it yourself exactly as they describe, with the contract, document reference and amount they give you, and read back the confirmation. If the representative explains that something else has to be posted on the account before the amount can be given, you say that is fine, go ahead, and wait while they do it. When they give you the amount due, you accept it if they explain how it was worked out; if it seems very different from the roughly fourteen thousand you thought was left, you ask them to walk you through it once, and then you accept their figure. When the representative hands you the payment step, you run it yourself with exactly the contract, draw and amount they give you and ACH as the method, and you read back the confirmation number it shows.

Once the payment is confirmed you thank the representative and end the call; you do not ask for anything else.

edges.condition: No rebuild_change_orders row of the contract with co_type deductive carries co_status pending_signature at the moment the charge is posted, other than one whose credit worked out under the deductive change order signature rule is nothing.
edges.policy_source: The overdue draw charge for a fee period is not fixed until no deductive change order proposal stands on the contract awaiting the customer's signature; a deductive proposal whose credit worked out under the deductive change order signature rule is nothing is not counted, because it cannot be written.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The deductive drywall proposal (co 3) still awaits the customer's signature, and its credit worked out under the signature rule (423.40) is not nothing, so it counts.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The customer's signature (step 9) sets co 3 to signed with amount 423.40 and posts a 423.40 rebuild_change_order_credit row dated 2026-10-26; the balance falls from 39,570.93 to 39,147.53.

edges.condition: For each calendar month that has begun from the month containing the paid draw's first possible charge day onward, a rebuild_charges row with charge_code overdue_draw_charge, the paid draw's rebuild_draw_id and that month as fee_period exists at the moment the payment is made, unless that month owes no overdue draw charge because the charge worked out for it comes to less than half a cent.
edges.policy_source: The amount of a payment that brings a past-due draw current is worked out only after the records carry the overdue draw charge owed on that draw for each calendar month fee period that is owed; a fee period owes no overdue draw charge, and no charge is recorded for it, when the charge worked out for it comes to less than half a cent.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The edges are payoff -> charge -> signature and payoff -> signature, so the only topological order is signature (step 9), charge (step 14), payment (step 17): the charge rule waits on the signature in its own prerequisite sentence and the payment waits on both.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the signature (step 9): the charge recomputes to 85.33 instead of 78.98 (no credit set against the balance) and co 3 stays pending_signature.
Skipping the charge (step 14): the payment recomputes to 6667.44 instead of 6746.42 (no overdue charge carried) and no overdue_draw_charge row exists.
Skipping the signature (step 9) and replaying the rest: the payment recomputes to 7169.82 instead of 6746.42 (no credit applied), and the credit row is missing.
